title: Hash-bucket prober router with normalized acceptance and tiered degrade
creator: Aisha Park
description: Goal: Implement a lightweight hash-bucket prober router that issues compact prefill probes to a small-model tier, computes a normalized acceptance score, and decides whether to continue full decode on the fast-path model or gracefully degrade through a tiered fallback chain. This is aimed at reducing average token cost while preserving p95/p99 latency SLOs. The design ties routing decisions to kernel selection fingerprints so we can prefer model variants whose kernels and attention kernels are optimal for the current input shape.
technical_design:
1) Hash-bucket prober: deterministic lightweight prefill that samples a short prefix (1-8 tokens hashed into buckets) to select a candidate model variant group. Bucketing reduces state and enables cheap per-shard routing decisions.

2) Normalized acceptance metric (NAM): a calibrated score in [0,1] that combines: early-output agreement (between probe and full-model logits), kernel-affinity penalty (if selected model's kernel mismatches preferred kernels for sequence length), and confidence variance (entropy-based). NAM is normalized by historical per-bucket baseline to account for prompt distribution skew.

3) Kernel-aware routing: maintain a small table mapping model-variant -> kernel-fingerprint and estimated kernel cost (GPU/SM throughput for typical seq-len). NAM is adjusted downward for variants with poor kernel affinity.

4) Tiered degrade plan: fast-path (preferred served variant) -> fallback-1 (quantized small variant with grouped attention kernels) -> fallback-2 (cached-prefix-resolve + remote-hosted API). Each fallback step has a time budget and acceptance threshold.

5) Prefill/decode scheduling: run a prefill probe and kick off a speculative partial decode concurrently. The scheduler aligns KV cache versions: probe writes go to ephemeral KV and are merged only if acceptance passes to avoid cache contamination. If NAM indicates high confidence before token T_thresh, commit speculative decode; else trigger fallback policies.

6) Observability: expose NAM, kernel-fingerprint, bucket-id, probe-latency, and commit decision in trace spans and dashboards for debugging and calibration.
acceptance_criteria: NAM computed for >98% of routed requests (failure modes logged, not blocking)
End-to-end p95 latency not worse than current baseline (<= baseline + 5ms) for 99% traffic during canary
Token cost reduction >= 8% on mixed web-chat workload in staging (measured by token-GPU-seconds)
Fallback chain triggers correctly and preserves output consistency 99% of the time (automated diff tests)
Trace fields (bucket_id, nam_score, kernel_fingerprint, decision) present in 100% of traces for routed requests
testing_plan: Unit tests for bucket hashing, NAM formula, and kernel-fingerprint table updates
Integration test that simulates KV cache isolation and commit/rollback between probe and decode
Load test in staging with 200 RPS mixed prompts to validate p95/p99 and cost metrics
A/B experiment comparing baseline routing vs hash-bucket router on real traffic (2% traffic) with automatic rollback if regressions detected
Automated output-regression tests using curated prompt set (pass rate >= 99% for top-k tokens)
rollout_plan: Internal canary: 0.5% of traffic in staging -> validate traces and dashboards (48h)
External canary: 2% of production traffic for 72h with automatic rollback on regression
Gradual ramp to 25% over 1 week if metrics stable, then to 100% by release window
Post-rollout: 7-day monitoring of cost, latency, and customer-facing error rate
perf_expectations: Expect 6-12% token-cost savings on conversational workloads with a neutral or slightly improved p50 latency. p95 should be unchanged; p99 protected by fallback time budgets. Prefill probe overhead should be <1ms median and <5ms 95th on typical GPU instances.

notes: Tradeoffs: hash-bucket probing reduces memory and decision latency but can amplify prompt distribution bias; normalization per-bucket mitigates this. Kernel-aware penalty intentionally sacrifices some NAM for variants with poor kernel throughput to avoid surprising latency regressions. Next steps: finalize NAM calibration strategy (offline histograms vs online exponential smoothing) and implement rollout kill-switch that disables speculative commit but leaves probes enabled for telemetry.
